about: The great beings of the world (powers wave 1, docs/design/powers.md): the legends, each one of a kind (one holder), each with a title, the strongest beings on the continent and national threats whose power could threaten the world; each a hand-written character sheet. level is before its titles' buffs (the owner's levels, stretched by order 92 so that countless more monsters fit below them, every legend's level x 1000/800 (D-185): Sarnavoth at 1000, by far the strongest single being, yet at a slight disadvantage against the three Primordial Archdemons (963-975) together; the Sword Saint about 875, an even match for one of them through his class, titles, skills and sword; the Lord of the Sea about 863, below him; every other legend between, from 800 up). home.type: lair (a fixed place it guards), roam (moves through its ground), city (lives among people, unknown), realm (serves a crown), sea (sleeps in the deep, rises at a coast), sealed (bound in a place); home.terr and home.place (a named place) let the final map place it in one pass. A sleeper (sleeper: true) sleeps for ages and decides once a year, through A.WHY, whether what would wake it (wake) has come. temper: A.WHY's ten axes (-1..1). habits: what each season draws it to and why. loves and grudges point at a realm (POL-xx), a people (race) or another being, with a weight and the reason; desires and fears are tags the module reads. skills: rank D to S, level 1 to 10 at most (past 10 a skill only evolves or merges); fight skills make its art (data/power.json power). items: each with a quality and what it gives. class: a being's calling, where it has one. reacts: how it answers being sought, flattered, attacked (challenged) or ignored. A title marked born was had from birth. Title requirements (req) are never shown to the player.

legends.age: about two thousand four hundred years

home.what: a split peak of the Dragon Mountains whose snow never stays, over a hall of melted coin

legends.history: Hatched in the first age, when the western realms were still tribes around fires. She took tribute from the first kings of Aldmark eighteen centuries ago and burned the ninth town that stopped paying; the chronicles of four realms begin their years from that fire. She has outlived every dynasty that ever paid her.
traits: speaks only to those who kneel

loves.why: the hoard is her history; each cup is a town

grudges.why: Aldmark's emperors stopped the tribute three reigns ago
a dwarf king once cut a scale from her flank while she slept

legends.speech: Slow, ornate, every sentence a reminder of a debt. Calls men 'little tithe'.

spring.why: she wakes lean and takes the herds of the high valleys

summer.why: she counts the hoard and suns herself on the peak

autumn.why: she feeds before the long sleep

winter.why: she sleeps curled on the coin until the thaw

legends.century: To have Aldmark's crown in her hoard and an emperor to bring it.

sought.line: She asks what you have brought. If it is nothing, she asks what you are worth.

flattered.line: She likes her name said well. She lets you go, this once, and remembers your face.

attacked.line: She does not hurry. She burns the hill you stand on.

ignored.line: An insult. A tithe is owed by whoever passes her shadow.

legends.d: The oldest dragon of the Dragon Mountains, grey-gold and long as a church. Nine towns are ash because their lords thought a tithe could be skipped.

skills.does: A breath that burns a town in a pass.
She knows every cup in her hoard and the town it came from; a thief is never safe.
A downbeat that flattens a camp.
Lords pay rather than fight.

items.does: Nine towns' gold, fused into one floor. Gives nothing in a fight; everything in pride.

home.what: the cold trench under the southern sea

legends.history: The sea-folk of the south say she made the shoals and keeps them. Twice in written memory she has risen: the first time the harbour of old Tamar went under, the second time the fishing fleets of three realms came home full for twenty years.

loves.why: they leave the first catch of the year on the water for her

grudges.why: Tamar's galleys netted the spawning grounds bare

legends.speech: She does not speak in words. Sailors hear her in the swell, and understand.

spring.why: the spawning season: she sleeps beneath it and guards it

autumn.why: the autumn gales stir the trench and sometimes her

winter.why: deep and cold, she sleeps the hardest

legends.century: To see the shoals full again, whatever stands on the shore.

sought.line: You row out over the trench. Nothing happens, for a long time. Then the sea grows very still.

flattered.line: Words mean nothing to the sea.

attacked.line: The swell rises like a hill. Your boat is not there afterwards.

ignored.line: She lets the small pass. The sea is wide.

legends.d: The Lord of the Sea, whom fishermen call the Tide-Mother: they say the southern sea is her back. She sleeps for decades. When she wakes, harbours drown and the shoals come home. Vast, old and slow; what she has of art is the sea's own.

skills.does: The sea rises where she wills: harbours drown.
A body the size of an island; most blows are lost in it.
Every fish and sea-beast near comes to her.
She is slow to rouse and slow to strike.

legends.age: nine centuries since it first thought

home.what: a black mere where an abbey once stood; the bell tower still leans out of it
home.place: the mere of the drowned abbey

legends.history: Nine hundred years ago it was a puddle in the cellar of an abbey that the marsh swallowed. It ate the library with the monks, and with the books it learned to think. It rose through every form a slime can take, one drowned century at a time, and it has wanted more books ever since.
traits: keeps its word to the letter

loves.why: they bring it books and it lets them read its own

grudges.why: the Church burned the shore of its mere to drive it off

legends.speech: Bubbles that shape words a beat late, in the voice of a long-dead librarian. Asks questions back.

spring.why: the thaw brings drowned things and careless travellers

summer.why: it grows in the warm months and must feed the growth

autumn.why: scholars come before the roads close; it trades

winter.why: it thickens under the ice and reads

legends.century: To learn what lies in the libraries of Irondeep and the elves, by trade or by swallowing them.

sought.line: It asks what you know. If you know something it does not, you may leave.

flattered.line: 'Kind,' it says. 'Now tell me something true.'

attacked.line: It flows over the bank faster than a man runs.

ignored.line: It watches you go, and wonders where.

legends.d: It began as a puddle in a drowned abbey and ate the library with the monks. It still reads what it eats. It bargains for books.

skills.does: It flows over a man and he is gone.
It knows what it ate: spells, histories, the weak points of men.
skills.from: evolved from Mindless Hunger, through every form of its line

skills.does: Steel that strikes it is eaten.

legends.age: older than the elves' coming west, some five thousand years

home.what: a hill whose door is only there at dusk

legends.history: She held court in the hills before the elves came west, and the elves made their first treaty with her, not with each other. Every hundred years she takes a mortal child into the hill as the treaty allows. The elves have never broken it. Men keep forgetting it exists.
values: a bargain kept to the letter

loves.why: the elves kept the first treaty for a thousand years

grudges.why: Northreach's lords cut her oaks for ships
the dead king walked through her dance and did not bow

legends.speech: Light, exact, every promise weighed. Never says 'thank you', which would be a debt.

spring.why: the dances of the new year draw her court above ground

summer.why: midsummer is her feast; mortals who stumble in dance until they drop

autumn.why: the wild hunt rides at the turning of the year

winter.why: the hill closes; the court sleeps until the thaw

legends.century: To bind a crown of men to a treaty as the elves are bound.

sought.line: She will hear you, at a price named before you speak.

flattered.line: She laughs, and the laugh is a gift. Do not thank her.

attacked.line: The hill opens. You are in her court now, for as long as she likes.

ignored.line: A path you know turns under your feet. She wants to see if you notice.

legends.d: Her court dances under a hill whose door is only there at dusk. Every bargain she makes she keeps to the letter, and so must you.

skills.does: What you see is what she wants: your blade strikes air.
Her court rides with her.
A promise made to her binds the body.

items.does: Whatever wears it serves her for a year and a day.

home.what: the barrow-roads of the old steppe
home.place: the barrow-roads of the old steppe

legends.history: A khan of the old steppe two thousand years ago, betrayed by his sons and buried alive with his guard. He would not lie down. Each winter his barrow-host walks the old roads looking for the realm he lost, and each autumn there are more of them, for those he kills rise behind him. The sons' line still rules in Qadir.
values: the old law of the steppe

loves.why: the orcs of the steppe still pour milk on the old barrows

grudges.why: Qadir stands on his stolen pastures, ruled by the line of the sons who buried him
the fey queen's court laughed at his host

legends.speech: The creak of old leather and a voice from under earth. Gives orders. Never asks.

spring.why: the thaw softens the barrows; he lies in his

summer.why: the long days keep the dead below

autumn.why: the nights grow; the host gathers on the old roads

winter.why: the dark months are his; the host rides on the living

legends.century: To sit again on the white felt of the steppe, over a host of every man Qadir has buried.

sought.line: He asks your lineage. If it is the wrong one, the host closes.

flattered.line: 'The living lie,' says the voice under the earth.

attacked.line: The host turns as one. There are many more than you counted.

ignored.line: Every rider who crosses the barrow-road owes the dead a horse.

legends.d: A king of the old steppe who would not lie down. Each winter his barrow-host walks, and each autumn there are more of them.

skills.does: Every man he kills rises behind him.
The old steppe cut, from the saddle.
His touch numbs the living.

items.does: The felt he was buried on; while he sits on it, he is king.

items.n: A sabre of the old steppe

home.what: the storm-front; she nests wherever the lightning falls

legends.history: A storm roc who outgrew her kind eleven hundred years ago. The herdsmen of the steppe have paid her a horse a household each summer for longer than they have had written laws; the year the khans refused, she sat on the clouds over their camp for a month and the lightning did not stop.

loves.why: Zanara's herdsmen have never missed the summer horse

grudges.why: Gorath's archers shot her mate out of the sky

legends.speech: Shrieks that break into words. Short, loud, impatient.

spring.why: she rides the spring storms to the north

summer.why: the herds are fat and the tribute is due

autumn.why: the autumn gales carry her south

winter.why: she sits out the winter in a high nest and lets no one near it

legends.century: To see Gorath's walls under her lightning.

sought.line: She screams for a horse. Then two.

flattered.line: She preens. She is fast, isn't she. You may go.

ignored.line: She dives past close enough to knock you flat, to see if you run.

legends.d: A bird the size of a barn whose wings bring the thunder. Herdsmen of the steppe pay her in horses, and she remembers who did not.

skills.does: Lightning from every wingbeat.
She flies in weather no bird lives through.
A stoop that breaks a horse's back.

legends.age: older than any throne of men: some four thousand years

home.what: the ridges; he sleeps standing, and is taken for a crag

legends.history: The eldest giant, who saw the first men climb into the mountains four thousand years ago and promised them passage if they kept the old peace: no forges on the high springs, no killing of the white goats. Three dynasties that broke that promise ended under rockfalls.

loves.why: the giant realms are his grandchildren's children
not love: an old wary respect between two who remember the same tribes

grudges.why: Emberdeep's dwarves put forges on the high springs

legends.speech: Very slow. Long silences. Calls everyone 'little cousin'.

spring.why: he walks the ridges to see the springs run clean

summer.why: he follows the white goats to the summer pastures

autumn.why: he stands over the passes before the snow

winter.why: he stands still on a ridge and sleeps through the snows

legends.century: To see the old peace kept for one more century, and the forges off the springs.

sought.line: He listens a whole afternoon, then answers in one word.

flattered.line: 'Little cousin, the mountain does not need praise.'

attacked.line: He lifts a boulder the size of a cottage.

ignored.line: He watches you pass as he watched your grandfathers.

legends.d: The eldest giant, older than any throne of men. He walks the ridges and keeps old promises. Breaking one has ended three dynasties.

skills.does: He hits like a rockfall.
A broken promise to him makes him twice as strong against the breaker.
He sleeps standing, taken for a crag.

items.n: A club of a whole pine

legends.history: The first of the frost wolves to take a mind, fifteen hundred years ago. She does not hunt men; she counts her children. A village that killed a whole pack in the hungry winter of the plague years was found empty in the spring, its doors open, every dog gone with the wolves.
values: the old balance of herd and hunter

loves.why: the elves hunt only what they need

grudges.why: Aldmark pays a bounty on wolf ears

legends.speech: A woman's low voice from the trees, and the howls answering it. Asks what you have killed this year.

spring.why: the cubs are born; she guards the dens

autumn.why: she leads the packs after the herds

winter.why: the hungry months; she hunts so the packs need not come to the villages

legends.century: To end the wolf bounties, one realm at a time.

sought.line: Wolves circle you. She asks what you have killed this year, and whether it was hungry.

flattered.line: She is not a dog to be praised.

attacked.line: The forest is full of eyes.

ignored.line: A lone traveller is no threat to the packs.

legends.d: A white wolf that walks among the packs like a queen. Kill her children in a cruel winter and she comes for your village with all of them.

skills.does: Every wolf of the north answers her.
A bite that freezes the blood.
She finds anything that walks.

legends.age: came through the gate some three thousand years ago

home.what: a merchant's house in a great town, behind a counting-room that is always open

legends.history: One of the three Primordial Archdemons, the first things that ever were on the far side of the gates. A sorcerer-prince opened the seventh gate three thousand years ago to win a war, and died owing him; Morvane stayed to collect. Ghazrul and Vethrael came through with him. Eighty years ago the Sword Saint sealed Ghazrul under the Burning Waste and cut Morvane's first face from him; Morvane was cleverer, and was never found again. He has worn a merchant's face in some great town ever since, lending at honest rates. His debtors do not die. They change.

grudges.why: the Church has burned three of his houses
the Saint sealed Ghazrul and cut Morvane's first face from him

legends.speech: Warm, reasonable, a little amused. Always offers terms. Never raises his voice.

summer.why: he dines with lords who owe him

winter.why: the long nights, when debts are collected

legends.century: To hold the debt of a crown and the crown with it.

sought.line: He offers you a chair and a loan, at very fair rates.

flattered.line: He smiles. 'And what would you like, for that compliment?'

attacked.line: The merchant's face slides off like a mask.

ignored.line: He makes a note of your name.

legends.d: He wears a merchant's face in some great town and lends at honest rates. His debtors do not die. They change.

skills.does: Every debtor owes him a share of their strength; he draws on all of them in a fight.
He wears any face he has taken; no one sees him coming.
Black fire from the seventh gate, enough to empty a street.
A bargain offered so well it is hard to refuse.

items.does: A merchant's book in which every debt he is owed is written in the debtor's blood.

home.what: the gate of a crown that paid its dwarf makers
home.place: the gate of its crown's capital

legends.history: Rune-iron the height of three men, made by dwarf smiths in the second age for a crown that paid them in full. That crown is long gone; the Warden serves whatever crown holds its gate, and asks only that its oath be read aloud each year at midwinter. It has heard the oath read by sixty-one rulers.
traits: lonely in a way it cannot name

loves.why: its makers; it bows to any dwarf smith

legends.speech: A voice like a bell under water. Answers only what is asked, word for word.

spring.why: the oath binds it to the gate

summer.why: the oath binds it to the gate

autumn.why: the oath binds it to the gate

winter.why: the oath is read at midwinter; it listens for it

legends.century: To hear its oath read every midwinter of the century.

sought.line: It asks your business at the gate, and waits for a true answer.

flattered.line: It does not understand the words, and waits.

attacked.line: It steps from the gate. The ground shakes once per step.

ignored.line: Its eyes follow you, and nothing else moves.

legends.d: Rune-iron the height of three men, made by dwarf smiths for a crown that paid them. It serves that realm's ruler, whoever holds the crown.

skills.does: While its oath is read each year, it does not tire or break.
At its gate nothing passes.
A blow that cracks walls.

items.does: Dwarf rune-iron, unbroken in eighteen centuries.
Its oath, read aloud each midwinter.

home.what: the dune roads between the oases
home.place: the dune roads of the south

legends.history: A lion of the deep desert that drank from a spring of fire fourteen hundred years ago and did not die. The caravans pray to him at the dune shrines; he lets the faithful cross and hunts the rest. He once spared a whole caravan because its youngest drover sang to him.

grudges.why: Sahrim's priests called him a devil and broke a shrine

legends.speech: A roar that is also a voice. Asks for a song.

spring.why: he walks the caravan roads as they open

summer.why: the white heat; he sleeps in a dune's shade

autumn.why: the herds come down to the oases

winter.why: the cool months bring pilgrims to his shrines

legends.century: To be worshipped from the Sunwall to the sea.

sought.line: He asks you for a song. A bad one ends the conversation.

flattered.line: He purrs like an avalanche. You may cross.

ignored.line: No one crosses his road without a word to him.

legends.d: A lion of fire that the caravans pray to. He lets the faithful cross and hunts the rest. In the summer heat he sleeps in the dunes.

skills.does: He burns like noon: the sand under you catches.
A lion's courage; he never yields.
Across a dune in one leap.

home.what: the high ice, where the glaciers begin
home.place: the high ice of the north

legends.history: The winter given a will. The giants of Frostholm and Hrimfell named their realms for her and leave her the first snow-lamb of each year. When the southern realms began to burn the northern forests for charcoal, the summers got shorter.
traits: merciless when the snow is defied

loves.why: the giants still leave her the first snow-lamb

grudges.why: Northreach's charcoal-burners eat the northern forests
the dragon's fire melted the glacier-mouth of the Crown Range

legends.speech: A whisper of snow. Few words, all of them cold.

spring.why: the thaw drives her up into the high ice

summer.why: she sleeps in the glacier's heart through the warm months

autumn.why: the first snows carry her down the valleys

winter.why: the dark months are hers; she walks into the lowlands

legends.century: To bring the snow to the southern sea once more, as it was before men.

sought.line: The wind rises and fills your tracks behind you.

flattered.line: The cold eases a little, to see what you do with it.

ignored.line: The snow falls, and goes on falling.

legends.d: The winter given a will. When she walks out of the high ice, harvests fail three valleys away and the wolves come down.

skills.does: The cold itself: rivers freeze, armies starve.
She is snow; a blade passes through.
The wolves come down with her.

home.what: a hall under the highest peak of the Dragon Mountains, sealed by his own fallen roof

legends.history: The first dragon hatched of the first clutch, who gathered every dragon of the age under one crown and ruled the skies of the north for two thousand years. Sixty years ago he met the Sword Saint on the ridge now called the Saint's Stair. The fight lasted three days. The Saint struck the last blow and the King fell into the mountain, roof and all; he has slept there wounded ever since, healing. Every dragon alive is his subject or his grandchild, and Vaskareth his eldest.
traits: remembers every insult for a thousand years

grudges.why: the only being who ever struck him down
Skyhold's monks built their monastery on his roof

legends.speech: Courtly and old, like a king addressing a petitioner. Calls the Saint 'my only equal' and no one else anything at all.

spring.why: he sleeps wounded under the fallen mountain

summer.why: he sleeps wounded under the fallen mountain

autumn.why: he sleeps wounded under the fallen mountain

winter.why: he sleeps wounded under the fallen mountain

legends.century: To wake healed and finish the fight on the Saint's Stair before the old man dies of years and robs him of it.

sought.line: An eye the size of a door opens in the rock. He asks whose sword you carry.

flattered.line: He has been praised by kings. You are not one.

ignored.line: He is asleep. You are lucky.

legends.d: The King of Dragons, by far the strongest being in the world, who ruled the north sky for two thousand years until the Sword Saint threw him under the Dragon Mountains sixty years ago. He sleeps there, healing. Every dragon alive is his subject.

skills.does: The breath of the first dragon: a mountainside melted, a host gone. Raw firepower beyond any other being.
He is the sky over the north; nothing outflies him.
Scales that turned every blade of every age but one.
Every dragon in sight obeys him.
Two thousand years of war: he knows every trick.

items.n: The Crown of the First Clutch
items.does: A ring of fused gold and dragon-bone set on his brow at his crowning.
The one cut that ever reached him, across the throat-scales. Not healed in sixty years.

home.what: under the Burning Waste, beneath a seal of glass the Saint cut into the sand

legends.history: The second Primordial Archdemon, who came through the seventh gate with Morvane and Vethrael three thousand years ago and burned her way across the south for the better part of that time. Eighty years ago the Sword Saint met her in what was then a green country; when it was over the country was the Burning Waste and she was under it, bound by a seal of glass. The sand above it is still warm.

loves.why: her brother, who has never tried to free her

grudges.why: he bound her under the sand
the Saint was one of them

legends.speech: Heat and a voice in it, saying the same few words over and over: open, open, open.

summer.why: bound under the seal; the sand is hottest

legends.century: To break the seal and unmake the realms of men.

sought.line: The sand speaks. It offers anything, everything, for a crack in the glass.

ignored.line: The heat follows you for a day.

legends.d: The second Primordial Archdemon, bound under the Burning Waste by the Sword Saint eighty years ago. The sand over the seal is still warm.

skills.does: A breath of white fire that leaves glass where a country was. Raw firepower without equal among the demons.
Wounds close as they open; she has never lost a limb for long.
A cone of burning sand.
Lesser beings flee or kneel.

items.does: The seal that binds her; while it holds, she does not leave the sand.

legends.age: one hundred and nineteen years; his strength has kept him alive long past any man

home.what: a shepherd's hut on the Saint's Stair, the ridge of the Dragon Mountains where he fought the King of Dragons
home.place: the Saint's Stair in the Dragon Mountains

legends.history: A shepherd's son of the western hills, born in a year of famine, who learned the sword from a deserter for a sack of oats. By thirty no one alive could stand against him. At thirty-nine he bound the Archdemon Ghazrul under the Burning Waste and cut the first face from Morvane. At fifty-nine he climbed the ridge to meet Sarnavoth, King of Dragons, alone, as he had promised; three days later the King was under the mountain. That was sixty years ago. He has lived on the ridge since, keeping goats and keeping watch, refusing every crown that has been offered. He is very old now, and still the strongest man alive: his class, Sword Saint, is the strongest one-to-one art there is, and no single being has outlasted him blade to blade.
traits: unbending once he has given his word

loves.why: his own people, whom he never stopped defending
the hills he was born in lie under Aldmark

grudges.why: four realms burned
the one who got away

rivals: Sarnavoth, King of Dragons, his only equal, asleep under the peak he watches
Ghazrul the Unmaker, whom he bound
Vethrael, who has never dared come near him
Ossery the Black, a swordsman of the south who challenged him nine times, lost nine times, and is buried at the foot of the ridge

sword.d: a plain grey blade that, the songs say, cut the seal of glass into the sand and the dragon-king's scales alike. He still carries it.

sayings: A sword is a promise you keep with your hands.
I have never fought a man who was not better than me at something.
The first cut is the one you decided on yesterday.
Go home. Your mother is waiting.
places: the Saint's Stair, the ridge where he lives
Vardan's Ford, where he held a river against a host alone
the Glass Seal in the Burning Waste
Oat Hill, where he took his first lesson
the Weeping Stone, where Ossery the Black wept after his ninth defeat

tellings.human: The shepherd's son who became the greatest swordsman who ever lived, threw the King of Dragons under the mountain, and still lives up on the ridge, an old man keeping watch.
tellings.elf: A man who lived as if he had four hundred years instead of sixty, and so learned in sixty what we learn in four hundred. Now he has had more than a hundred, and the elves send their best blades to sit with him.
tellings.dwarf: A man who never once broke his word. The dwarves carve his saying over their forges and send him a new kettle every ten years, which he never uses.
tellings.orc: The orcs tell that their champions fought him and lost with honour, and that he once shared bread with a beaten khan. They call him the Grey Brother, and say he will die standing.
tellings.giant: The giants say he is not a man at all but a mountain that stood up for a while, and is sitting on itself now, waiting.

legends.end: His age has not ended. He sits outside his hut on the ridge in the evenings with Morrowglass across his knees, watching the peak the King fell under. The pilgrims who climb to him say his hands still do not shake.
legends.speech: Quiet, plain, a hill-shepherd's words, slower now. Never boasts. Asks people their names, and their mothers'.

spring.why: the kids are born; he tends the goats on the ridge

summer.why: he walks down to the valley villages once a year, to see the people

autumn.why: he watches the peak the King fell under

winter.why: he sits by his fire with the sword across his knees

legends.century: To see the King of Dragons stay under his mountain until the day he himself dies, and to find someone worth teaching first.

sought.line: He asks your name and your mother's, then hands you a stick and asks you to show him how you stand.

flattered.line: "Go home," he says. "Your mother is waiting."

attacked.line: He does not draw. He takes your blade from your hand with two fingers and gives it back.

ignored.line: He nods to you as you pass, as he nods to everyone.

legends.d: Cael Vardan, the Sword Saint: a shepherd's son who became the greatest swordsman of any age, bound an Archdemon and threw the King of Dragons under the mountain. He is a hundred and nineteen, lives on the ridge where he fought, and is still the strongest man alive. His class is Sword Saint, the strongest one-to-one combat art there is. Every child knows his story.

skills.does: The class itself, the strongest one-to-one art there is: every cut is the one the foe did not guard, and no single being has outlasted him blade to blade.
A cut that parts what should not part: scale, ward, seal and spell alike. Once a fight; nothing it touches mends that day.
skills.from: merged from Hill-Shepherd's Sword and the Glass Cut, both at level 10

skills.does: He is never rushed: no feint, fear or fury moves him before he means to move.
He tires slower than stone erodes. A long fight is his ground.

items.does: A plain grey blade that cut the seal into the sand and the dragon-king's scales.
Sixty years on the ridge. It gives nothing but warmth.

home.what: the pilgrim roads, in the shape of a hooded singer

legends.history: The third of the Primordial Archdemons, who came through the seventh gate with Morvane and Ghazrul and has never once been seen fighting. Vethrael collects voices. Each soul it takes keeps singing inside it, and the choir is now some hundred thousand strong. It walks the pilgrim roads as a hooded singer; villages where it sings at a funeral are quiet for a generation afterwards.

loves.why: her rage is a sound it admires

grudges.why: the elves sing better than its choir and will not join it
he bound its sister and silenced a road it loved

legends.speech: A hundred voices in one, very soft, always in tune. Asks you to sing.

summer.why: the summer festivals, where it sings

autumn.why: the funerals of the hungry season

winter.why: it rests in a ruined chapel and listens to its choir

legends.century: To add a royal voice to the choir, and then a whole court.

sought.line: It offers to teach you a song no living man knows, for one note of your voice.

flattered.line: It thanks you in your dead mother's voice, and walks on.

attacked.line: The choir sings, all of it at once.

ignored.line: It hums a tune from your childhood until you turn around.

legends.d: The third Primordial Archdemon, who walks the pilgrim roads as a hooded singer and takes the voices of the dead. A hundred thousand souls sing inside it.

skills.does: A hundred thousand voices sing at once: the ground shakes, glass and minds break as far as the eye can see.
One note that silences a heart.
Speaks in the voices of your dead; the will fails.
Seen as a hooded singer, harmless.

items.n: A pilgrim's staff of black wood
